rules.claim: The Download action is a detail GET action on DocumentViewSet. It delegates to file_response(pk, request, "attachment"); exceptions for missing files or missing documents are converted to Http404.

file_response first resolves the path-selected request document and its root document with include_deleted=True; a forbidden response terminates before file selection, otherwise it computes the effective file document and calls serve_file.
The resource whose source/archive file can be opened is file_doc returned by _get_effective_file_doc(resolved.request_doc, resolved.root_doc, request), not automatically the path-identified document.
rules.resource: effective document selected for file serving

rules.claim: The resolver loads request_doc by id=pk from Document.global_objects because file_response calls it with include_deleted=True, derives root_doc with get_root_document(include_deleted=True), and then evaluates the explicit permission check.

When request.user is non-None and has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, "view_document", root_doc) is false, the resolver returns HttpResponseForbidden("Insufficient permissions") and file_response returns that response without opening a file.
The resolver continues to file selection when request.user is None or the root-document permission helper returns true.

If the path-selected request_doc is itself a version (root_document_id is not None) and no version query parameter is supplied, the effective file document is request_doc; otherwise resolution proceeds from root_doc through _resolve_file_doc.

When the request_doc is the root document or a version parameter is present, _get_effective_file_doc delegates selection to _resolve_file_doc(root_doc, request), so the file document is resolved relative to the authorized root_doc.

def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)
